The United States Military Academy (USMA), commonly known as West Point,[7] is a United States service academy in West Point, New York, that educates cadets for service as commissioned officers in the United States Army.
The academy is located approximately 50 miles (80 km) north of New York City on the western bank of the Hudson River.
The academy is a direct reporting unit, and as such, the Superintendent reports directly to the Army Chief of Staff (CSA).[120][121]

Cadets attend the United States Military Academy free of charge, with all tuition and board paid for by the Army in return for a service commitment of five years of active duty and three years of reserve status upon graduation.[179]
West Point was first officially accredited in 1925, and in 1933 began granting Bachelor of Science degrees to all graduates.[58]
West Point admitted its first 119 female cadets in 1976.[74][75]

West Point is a highly residential baccalaureate college, with a full-time, four-year undergraduate program that emphasizes instruction in the arts, sciences, and professions with no graduate program.[141]
Regardless of major, all cadets graduate with a Bachelor of Science degree.[149]

West Point's academic program grants the Bachelor of Science degree with a curriculum that grades cadets' performance upon a broad academic program, military leadership performance, and mandatory participation in competitive athletics.
"Cadets" underwent training in artillery and engineering studies at the garrison since 1794.[18]

Congress formally authorized the establishment and funding of the school with the Military Peace Establishment Act of 1802, which Jefferson signed on 16 March.[2] The academy officially commenced operations on 4 July 1802.[22]

In 1817, Colonel Sylvanus Thayer became the Superintendent and established the curriculum, elements of which are still in use as of 2020[update]. Thayer instilled strict disciplinary standards, set a standard course of academic study, and emphasized honorable conduct.

The United States Military Academy (USMA), commonly known as West Point, is a federal service academy in West Point, New York, that prepares cadets for commissioned service in the United States Army. Its campus lies on the western bank of the Hudson River, approximately 50 miles north of New York City. The academy is a direct reporting unit, and its Superintendent reports directly to the Army Chief of Staff. Cadets attend a residential, four-year undergraduate program, with tuition and board funded by the Army in exchange for a service commitment.

Congress authorized the academy in legislation signed by Thomas Jefferson on 16 March 1802; operations began on 4 July that year. Earlier artillery and engineering training at the garrison dated from 1794. Under Sylvanus Thayer, who became Superintendent in 1817, the academy established a standardized curriculum and disciplinary framework. It was first officially accredited in 1925 and began awarding Bachelor of Science degrees to all graduates in 1933. Women first entered the academy in 1976.

The curriculum combines arts and sciences with military leadership and physical development. All graduates receive a Bachelor of Science degree regardless of major, and the institution has no graduate program. Its research centers cover subjects including cyber studies, contemporary conflict, engineering, and leadership. Enrollment was 4,389 cadets in the 2016–2017 academic year.
